headline: The only goal came from a VAR call the referees' body admitted was wrong

standfirst.text: City lost Phil Foden to a red card after 23 minutes and still won at Old Trafford.
Erling Haaland's 60th-minute winner was flagged offside, then given by VAR.
The same evening, Pro Ref contacted United to acknowledge "an error of judgement".

body.text: Haaland scored from close range after Joško Gvardiol's deflected cross, with Enzo Fernández in an offside position going for the ball ahead of him.
The flag went up. VAR found Haaland onside and let the goal stand because Fernández hadn't touched the ball.
Pro Ref's verdict: the VAR "did not recognise the likely impact of his position and should have recommended an on-field review".

decided.title: The red card: right, and costly for City

body.text: Foden kicked out at Bruno Fernandes and Michael Oliver sent him off. VAR confirmed it after a quick check.
ESPN's review said Foden "can have no complaints as he lost his composure" and praised Oliver's positioning.

decided.title: United couldn't use the extra man

body.text: Not an officiating issue, but it's part of the answer. United played more than an hour against ten men and didn't score.
Fans in the post-match thread said so too, even the ones angry at VAR: "the most inept display against 10 men I can remember."

bottomLine.text: Take the goal away and nobody scored. That's why the ledger marks the VAR call as match-deciding, and why it counts against the VAR and AVAR on Ref Watch.

timeline.text: Kick-off at Old Trafford. Michael Oliver referees, Matt Donohue is on VAR.
Foden sent off for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes. VAR confirms.
Haaland scores. The flag goes up, VAR overturns it and the goal stands.
Gary Neville on Sky: "There is no doubt that Enzo is attempting to play the ball and putting Lisandro Martinez off."
ESPN reports Pro Ref's statement: an "error of judgement", and contact made with United.
Wayne Rooney: "Not recognising that Fernandez was offside is simply staggering."
Donohue and AVAR Blake Antrobus left off the weekend's fixtures. They won't work a top-flight match until 10 October at the earliest.

points.text: Haaland himself was onside when the cross came in.
Fernández never touched the ball, so any offside offence was a judgement call, not a fact.
The VAR's reading: Fernández's position didn't stop Martínez playing the ball.
The law makes it offside to clearly attempt to play a ball that's close when that action impacts an opponent.
ESPN's review: "Martinez's ability to defend the ball was certainly affected by Fernández."
Neville: "There is no doubt that Enzo is attempting to play the ball and putting Lisandro Martinez off."

resolution.text: Pro Ref sided with the case against. The VAR should have sent Oliver to the monitor.

arguments.question: Should Bruno Fernandes have been punished too?

points.text: Enzo Maresca accepted Foden's red but argued Fernandes should have been sent off as well.
One fan in the thread: Bruno's part was no more than a yellow, "which was missed".
Foden kicked out; ESPN's review said that kind of action very likely ends in a red for violent conduct.
VAR looked at the incident and only confirmed the red for Foden.

resolution.text: Still open. There's no panel ruling on Fernandes on record yet.

a.text: The assistant flagged him, but VAR checked and found Haaland onside when the cross was played.
The offside question that mattered was about Enzo Fernández, who was in an offside position and went for the ball before Haaland.

questions.q: How can Fernández be offside if he never touched the ball?

a.text: Touching the ball isn't required. A player in an offside position commits an offence if they clearly attempt to play a ball that's close and that action impacts an opponent.
Because Fernández didn't touch it, the call was subjective. Pro Ref said the VAR should have recommended an on-field review.

Matt Donohue and AVAR Blake Antrobus weren't given Premier League matches the following weekend. With the international break, they won't officiate a top-flight match until 10 October at the earliest.

questions.q: Was the red card the right call?

a.text: Yes, according to ESPN's review: Foden "can have no complaints as he lost his composure." Maresca agreed the red was correct, but thought Fernandes should have gone too.

questions.q: Has Michael Oliver refereed this derby before?

a.text: Not last season. Anthony Taylor refereed both 2025–26 league derbies: City 3–0 United in September and United 2–0 City in January. Oliver took eight league games involving one of the two clubs.
